## Solution

**Setup.** Place a coordinate axis along line $XY$ with $X$ at $0$ and $Y$ at $L = XY$.

**Power of a point.** Since $P$ lies on chord $AB$ (inside the circle), the power of $P$ is
$$PX \cdot PY = PA \cdot PB = 6 \cdot 5 = 30 \quad (\text{signed: } -30).$$
Likewise $Q$ lies on chord $CD$ (inside the circle), so
$$QX \cdot QY = QC \cdot QD = 7 \cdot 12 = 84 \quad (\text{signed: } -84).$$

**Equations.** Let $P$ be at coordinate $p$ and $Q$ at coordinate $q$ on the line. The signed products give:
$$p(p - L) = -30 \;\;\Longrightarrow\;\; L = p + \frac{30}{p},$$
$$q(q - L) = -84 \;\;\Longrightarrow\;\; L = q + \frac{84}{q}.$$
Also $|p - q| = PQ = 27$.

**Case 1: $p - q = 27$, i.e., $q = p - 27$.** Substituting into $L = p + 30/p = (p-27) + 84/(p-27)$:
$$\frac{30}{p} = -27 + \frac{84}{p-27}.$$
Clearing denominators: $(30 + 27p)(p - 27) = 84p$, which simplifies to
$$27p^2 - 783p - 810 = 0 \;\;\Longrightarrow\;\; p^2 - 29p - 30 = 0 \;\;\Longrightarrow\;\; (p-30)(p+1) = 0.$$
The root $p = -1$ places $P$ outside segment $XY$ (outside the circle), which is invalid. So $p = 30$, giving
$$L = 30 + \frac{30}{30} = 31.$$
Check: $q = 3$, $L = 3 + 84/3 = 31$. ✓

**Case 2: $q - p = 27$, i.e., $q = p + 27$.** By symmetry this yields $p = 1$, $q = 28$, and again $L = 31$.

**Verification.** With $X=0$, $Y=31$, $P=30$, $Q=3$: $PX \cdot PY = 30 \cdot 1 = 30$ ✓, $QX \cdot QY = 3 \cdot 28 = 84$ ✓, $PQ = 27$ ✓.

$$\boxed{XY = 31}$$
